blogTitle: The Case for Severus Snape (and other things I am right about)
about: Hi. I'm Maddie. I have read all six books 9 times each (book 5: 11 times, it rewards patience) and I'm the author of 'The Case for Severus Snape,' an 11-part essay series proving whose side he is really on. (Ours. Read Part 4 before you argue with me.) I have also sorted every resident of this site into a Hogwarts house using a 22-question rubric and direct observation. Your result is final. Appeals may be submitted in writing and will be denied. For the record, I am a Ravenclaw. The online quiz has said Hufflepuff 14 times in a row, which only proves the quiz can't handle people who would take a quiz 14 times. Book 7 has no title and no date yet. I am fine. I have a sealed envelope of predictions and a calendar.
aboutMore: Other facts, cited: I was number 41 in line at the Borders midnight release (wristband saved, taped inside my predictions notebook). I finished Half-Blood Prince in 9 hours and 20 minutes. I'm reading the whole series out loud to my little brother Owen, who is 7, one chapter a night, with all the voices. We're on book 3. My Hagrid is terrible and he requests it anyway. Mom has banned Horcrux talk at the dinner table ever since The Incident (I brought diagrams) (there was gravy).
meet: J.K. Rowling, for exactly four questions (I've narrowed it down from 61). Whoever wrote the sorting quiz, for a meeting. The person at MuggleNet who reads the essay submissions, to ask if they got mine (all 11). And my brother in about four years, when he reaches chapter 27 and finally understands why I was like this.

keywords.harry potter: You said the words. Quick placement test: who gave Harry the map, and who MADE it? If you only know from the movies, that's ok, it isn't your fault, movie 3 never says. I have a handout.
keywords.hufflepuff: Hufflepuff is a GOOD house. Loyal, fair, hard-working, common room right next to the kitchens. I'm not saying that because of the quiz. I'm a Ravenclaw. But if I weren't, it would be fine. It would be completely fine.

bulletins.subject: Book 7 Prediction Envelope: OFFICIALLY SEALED
bulletins.body: Let the record show that tonight I sealed 9 predictions for Book 7 in an envelope, signed across the flap, witnessed by my brother Owen (age 7, crayon). I won't list all nine, but for the record: (1) Snape has been on the right side the whole time. (2) R.A.B. is somebody's little brother and we already know his last name. (3) That locket nobody could open in book 5 mattered. (4) The scar is more than a scar. If I'm right, I'd like a small apology from everyone who said 'Maddie, you're reaching.' If I'm wrong about Snape, I will eat the envelope. That's how sure I am. The envelope is in my sock drawer. Leo, do not put my sock drawer on your board.

blog.title: The Case for Severus Snape, Part 11: You Don't Tutor Your Enemy
blog.body: Welcome back. If you're new, start at Part 1; I won't be recapping. EXHIBIT A: at the end of book 6, a certain professor is leaving a duel he could finish in about four seconds. What does he do instead? He blocks. And blocks. And then he gives ADVICE. He tells the person chasing him exactly what they're doing wrong, like it's a Tuesday and there's a quiz on Friday. Who tutors somebody they want to lose? EXHIBIT B: he has had six years of chances. Six. Nobody needs six years if they mean it. EXHIBIT C: Dumbledore trusted him and never told anyone why, and people keep calling that a hole in my argument. It isn't a hole. It's the entire next book. The message boards say I'm reaching. Mr. Feeney says I need a new topic. My brother says 'I hope he's nice.' I rest my case. (Part 12 is coming. I thought of something in the shower.)

blog.title: I waited in line for six hours and I would do it again tomorrow
blog.body: Since Book 7 has no date, I've been thinking about the last midnight release. Dad drove me to the Borders at 6 PM. I wore my robe (a graduation gown from the thrift store, hemmed with staples) and a Time-Turner made from a key ring and part of an egg timer. I was number 41 in line. The girl behind me thought Snape was evil, so we argued for two hours, and then she shared her jelly beans with me, so. At midnight they handed me the book and it was heavier than I expected, and I just stood there holding it in the parking lot. Dad didn't start the car. He said 'take your time, Mads.' I read by the dome light the whole way home and finished in 9 hours and 20 minutes. I cried at chapter 27, on the stairs, so Owen wouldn't hear. I still have the wristband. I'd wait in that line again tomorrow. I'd bring more snacks.

blog.title: Sorting Quiz, Attempt #14: An Official Complaint (and a confession)
blog.body: To whoever maintains the sorting quiz: I have now taken it 14 times and received Hufflepuff 14 times. I am a Ravenclaw. I read with highlighter tabs. I have written 11 essays nobody assigned. Your quiz is obviously weighted toward the 'would you share your dessert' question, which isn't fair, because of course I'd share my dessert, what kind of question is that. ...Ok. A confession, since this is my own blog. Tonight I was reading to Owen and he asked which house is the best one. I said Ravenclaw without thinking. He asked which house would help him find his other shoe. I said Hufflepuff. He asked which house I'd want next to me if I was scared. I said Hufflepuff again, pretty fast. He said 'so that one's the best one' and fell asleep. I'm still a Ravenclaw. I'm only saying the quiz may have been written by someone who has met me. Complaint withdrawn. For now.

survey.title: The Official Potter Fan Survey (answer honestly, I'll know)
qa: Favorite book?
Book 5. It's the longest and people say it's the angriest. Those are the same reason I like it.
Which house are u in?
Ravenclaw. (The quiz says otherwise. 14 times. The quiz and I are in talks.)
Favorite character?
Hermione. Then McGonagall. Then a third person I've written 11 essays about.
Least favorite character?
Umbridge. I had to put the book down and walk around the yard.
Who do u ship?
Ron and Hermione. Since the Yule Ball. I was right, I've been right for two whole books, and I've been very gracious about it.
Book or movie?
Book. In the book he asks CALMLY. I don't want to talk about it. (I'll talk about it for 20 minutes.)
What's ur wand made of?
Vine wood, ten and three-quarter inches. Yes, that's Hermione's. No, I'm not changing it.
What would u see in the Mirror of Erised?
Me, holding Book 7, next to an opened envelope of correct predictions. Also in the mirror my brother can read chapter books by himself.
Best class at Hogwarts?
Ancient Runes. Nobody ever says what happens in there and I need to know.
Ever cried at a book?
Chapter 27. On the stairs. Third stair from the top. It's still the best reading stair.
What would ur Patronus be?
An owl. Or, according to everyone who knows me, a badger. I'm not discussing it.
